title: Aify-style article index homepage
summary: This iteration lands the first agreed Aify-inspired slice after PR204: the homepage becomes a compact article library backed by public articles.json, the previous operational dashboard moves to ops.html, article records gain category, flavor, score, channel, company, and product metadata, and schema/unit/e2e/browser checks guard the new public contract.

lessons.lesson: The public reader surface needs an article-level database before deeper multi-agent workflow changes can show value.
lessons.evidence: The new build extracts and deduplicates article records across reports into docs/articles.json, then renders index.html from that normalized public contract instead of only from daily report pages.
lessons.recommended_action: Keep articles.json as the stable public data surface when implementing the next pipeline DAG stages.

lessons.lesson: Aify-style taxonomy is useful immediately even when generated heuristically from existing report artifacts.
lessons.evidence: Article records now carry domain, flavor, quality_score, importance, channels_l1, channels_l2, companies, and products, and tests verify the public schema does not leak internal generation fields.
lessons.recommended_action: Promote taxonomy and score assignment into isolated candidate-scoring and classification agents in the next workflow PR.

lessons.lesson: Homepage and operations dashboard should be separate products.
lessons.evidence: index.html now serves the reader-oriented article library, while ops.html preserves the prior dashboard for source, trend, and run-state inspection.
lessons.recommended_action: Keep daily report pages focused on narrative synthesis and keep operational diagnostics out of the first public viewport.

suggestions.issue: The production workflow is still not split into the full 15+ isolated stages requested by the product direction.
suggestions.evidence: This iteration intentionally limits scope to the article-index contract and frontend, while PR204 only partially stages collect, admit, summarize, assemble, audit, validate, and publish verification.
suggestions.suggestion: Implement the next PR as a pipeline DAG/state-machine refactor with explicit fetch, parse, score, classify, dedupe, cross-language matching, timeliness, quality review, correction, storage, card/page generation, delivery, and cleanup stages.
suggestions.expected_benefit: Reduces context contamination, increases parallelism, and makes failures inspectable at the same granularity as the Aify reference.
suggestions.promotion_path: Next project iteration after article-index homepage lands.

followups.action: Build the full multi-agent production DAG/state-machine on top of the new article-level contract, then re-check whether smaller source-quality followups still matter.
